battle.name: 太平天國起義
battle.brief: 一八五〇年一月洪秀全在廣西桂平金田舉旗起義，太平軍十四年轉戰半壁江山，一八六四年天京陷落。前期兩軍靠冷兵器與繳獲的舊式抬炮相持，線膛砲在太平軍手中幾乎絕跡；清方於六十年代自上海大量購入洋砲，蘇州與天京兩役的遠程砲火才真正壓垮城頭密集隊形。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 起義一方是建號太平天國的拜上帝會軍。洪秀全自稱天王，一八五三年定都南京後改名天京；楊秀清任東王總攬軍政，洪仁玕封干王主政，李秀成封忠王統兵，陳玉成封英王，石達開封翼王。軍隊編制分師、旅、營、卒數級，每營轄前、後、左、右四軍並設火器營，各級設軍帥、師帥、旅帥、營官，號令由天京以文書、印璽與諭旨下達，前線大軍多由王侯與元帥直接指揮。基層除主力正軍外，另有散兵與隨軍而行的鄉民、挑夫、船丁，攻城則設土營專司掘壕、架梯、運糧。清廷一方由中央的軍機處、戶部與各省督撫分節制：八旗、綠營守城守關，團練與練勇擔當野戰主力，地方督撫自籌糧餉、就地徵集。一八五二年詔令各省籌辦團練之後，曾國藩於一八五三年在湖南建湘軍，李鴻章於一八六二年起建淮軍，尚有胡林翼、曾國荃、李續賓、鮑超、多隆阿、江忠源、向榮等各領一路。一八六〇年之後，上海洋行大量售出洋槍洋砲，英人帶領的洋槍隊與常勝軍先後加入作戰，使天平在火力一端逐漸傾斜。
countriesEn: The side of the rising was the army of the God Worshippers' Society, which proclaimed the state of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Hong Xiuquan styled himself the Heavenly King, and after Nanjing fell in 1853 the city was renamed Tianjing and made his capital. Yang Xiuqing held the title of East King and ran the government, Hong Rengan was made King of Gan and took charge of state affairs, Li Xiucheng was made Loyal King and led the armies in the field, Chen Yucheng was made Heroic King, and Shi Dakai was made Wing King. The military organisation ran in graded steps of division, brigade, battalion and company; each battalion was split into front, rear, left and right columns with a fire support element, and the posts were filled by army commanders, division commanders, brigade commanders and battalion officers, with orders running from Tianjing by written dispatch, seal and mandate, while the great armies in the field were usually commanded directly by the princes and marshals. Below the regular army stood scattered bands together with the peasants, porters and boatmen who moved with it, and for siege work there were specialist earthwork units charged with digging ditches, raising ladders and carrying grain. The other side was the Qing court, with the Grand Council and the Ministry of Revenue at the centre and the provincial governors on the spot: banner troops and the Green Standard held towns and passes, while local militias and drill corps did the fighting in the field, each province raising its own money and men. After the court ordered provincial militias to be raised in 1852, Zeng Guofan formed the Xiang Army in Hunan in 1853, Li Hongzhang raised the Huai Army from 1862, and Hu Linyi, Zeng Guoquan, Li Xubin, Bao Chao, Dolong'a, Jiang Zhongyuan and Xiang Rong each took charge of a sector. After 1860 the foreign firms in Shanghai sold large quantities of foreign muskets and guns, and foreign rifle corps and the Ever Victorious Army joined the fighting in turn, so that the balance on the question of firepower steadily tipped towards the Qing.
people: 起義的發動者是廣東花縣人洪秀全。他科舉屢試不第，一八四三年讀到基督教勸世良言一類的書卷後立拜上帝會，以天父天兄救贖的說法聚眾；同窗馮雲山於一八四四年入廣西紫荊山傳教，一八五〇年冬病逝於蓑衣渡，會眾為之營葬山中。東王楊秀清原為西江船工出身，善於權變，一八五四年總理朝政，一八五六年的天京變亂中被殺。翼王石達開為廣西桂平客家人，是早期起義的核心將領，一八五六年間負氣率眾離天京出走，轉戰江西、雲南、四川，一八六三年五月在大渡河被俘，同月在成都被處死。忠王李秀成自廣東犍為加入太平軍，以善於帶兵作戰、能撫輯部眾著稱，一八五九年封忠王，一八六四年七月天京被圍時率大軍在外回援而不得入城，城破後被俘，遇害於南京。英王陳玉成自一八五六年之後獨當一面，屢破清軍於鄂、皖、蘇三省交界，一八六二年五月在湖北潁州被俘，押解途中為捻軍所劫，送回天京後被處死。干王洪仁玕一八四八年避居香港，至一八五一年始返桂歸附，一八五九年受封為王，所上資政新篇是太平天國唯一一套成體系的治國方案。北伐主將林鳳祥、李開芳於一八五三年率師出師，一八五五年兵敗被執。西征主將胡以晃、曾天養於一八五三年受命西進，後由石達開接統西征大軍。清方可用之人更多：江忠源首倡楚勇、率眾援廣西而殉，曾國藩以理學帶兵、創湘軍而終制平其勢，李鴻章接手淮軍與上海軍械洋務，曾國荃、彭玉麟、鮑超負責攻守與水師，胡林翼坐鎮湖北，李續賓、多隆阿、馮子材各當一面；英人戈登於一八六三年率常勝軍入華，參與攻蘇州與打太平餘部。
peopleEn: The man who set the rising in motion was Hong Xiuquan, a native of Huaxian in Guangdong. He failed the examinations repeatedly, and in 1843, after reading Christian tracts of the kind that includes the Good Words to Admit the Way of Salvation, he founded the God Worshippers' Society and gathered followers around the doctrine of redemption by the Heavenly Father and the Heavenly Brother. His schoolfellow Feng Yunshan entered the Zijing mountains of Guangxi to preach in 1844 and died of illness at Suoyidu in the winter of 1850, and his followers buried him in the hills. The East King, Yang Xiuqing, was a boatman from the west river who had risen through his wits and in 1854 took charge of the government, only to be killed in the Tianjing incident of 1856. The Wing King, Shi Dakai, a Hakka from Guiping in Guangxi, was a core commander of the early rising; in 1856 he left Tianjing in a fit of anger with a great part of the army, campaigned through Jiangxi, Yunnan and Sichuan, and in May 1863 was taken prisoner at the Dadu River and executed at Chengdu in the same month. The Loyal King, Li Xiucheng, had joined the movement from Qianwei in Guangdong and was known both for his generalship and for his way of holding his troops together; he was made Loyal King in 1859 and in July 1864, with Tianjing besieged, brought a great army to the relief of the city without being able to enter it, and after the city fell was taken prisoner and killed at Nanjing. The Heroic King, Chen Yucheng, commanded independently from 1856 and repeatedly broke Qing armies along the meeting line of Hubei, Anhui and Jiangsu; in May 1862 he was taken at Yingzhou in Hubei, was carried off by the Nian while on the road, and was put to death after being brought back to Tianjing. The King of Gan, Hong Rengan, had come late to the movement, was made a king in 1859, and his Zizheng Xinpian was the only coherent programme of government the Taiping ever produced. The commanders of the northern expedition, Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang, marched out in 1853 and were taken after their defeat in 1855. The commanders of the western campaign, Hu Huihuang and Zeng Tianyang, received their orders in 1853, and Shi Dakai later took over the great army of that campaign. The Qing had many more usable men: Jiang Zhongyuan first raised the Chu braves and marched to the relief of Guangxi, where he was killed; Zeng Guofan led his troops on the model of the classics, founded the Xiang Army and in the end brought the movement under control; Li Hongzhang took over the Huai Army and the Shanghai business of foreign arms and arsenals; Zeng Guoquan, Peng Yulin and Bao Chao handled the sieges and the river war; Hu Linyi sat at the centre in Hubei; Li Xubin, Dolong'a and Feng Zicai each held a section; and the Englishman Gordon brought the Ever Victorious Army into the country in 1863, taking part in the attack on Suzhou and in the pursuit of the Taiping remnants.
kits: 本卡線膛砲是十九世紀中葉歐洲新出的前裝線膛野砲，以小口徑銅砲配專屬藥包，射程遠、精度高，野戰時一門砲便能壓住步兵射程以外的地帶。普魯士自一八四〇年代起研究膛線與藥包配合，至一八五〇年代初已有六磅與十二磅的前裝線膛砲問世；一八五三至一八五六年的克里米亞戰爭中，英法聯軍以線膛砲對付俄軍的舊式滑膛要塞砲，射程優勢極為明顯，此後線膛野砲逐步取代滑膛炮，成為歐洲陸軍野戰的新標準。太平軍手中線膛砲極少：起義初期所戰皆為冷兵器，大刀、長矛、叉、標槍配合火繩或燧發的鳥槍與抬炮；一八五三年攻入南京時繳獲清廷與地方官僚所存的銅鐵大砲、抬炮、火藥與大批彈藥，數目以數百計，但多屬滑膛短管，射擊平直、射程有限，既無專職砲兵，也無統一射擊規程，往往隨意架於城頭或營壘發放。城頭密集隊形要靠這樣的舊砲反擊遠程精確射擊，幾乎無從辦到。清方則自一八六〇年第二次鴉片戰爭後，經上海洋行大量購入洋槍與洋砲，一八六三年設蘇州洋炮局，一八六五年江南製造總局開辦，一八六七年天津機器局繼起，線膛砲與洋槍逐步列裝湘軍與淮軍，並編成砲隊。除此之外，攻城器械有雲梯、攻門槌、壕溝、地道與爆破，湘軍曾以地道爆破攻破江西吉安、瑞州、撫州等城；水師方面，太平軍在長江下游集結數百舟船、設水營行軍，清方有長江水師與湘軍水師；運輸依賴糧臺、夫役與漕運，太平軍則以徵糧與聖庫制應付軍需。馬匹是雙方初期都缺乏的資源，太平軍騎兵多由粵桂舊部與徵集的馬匹組成，湘軍亦以輕騎追擊為主。
kitsEn: The rifled field gun on this card was the new muzzle-loading rifled field piece of mid-nineteenth century Europe: a small calibre bronze gun firing its own prepared cartridge, with long range and good accuracy, so that a single gun in the field could command ground beyond the reach of infantry. Prussia began working on the combination of rifling and prepared ammunition in the 1840s, and by the early 1850s six-pounder and twelve-pounder muzzle-loading rifled guns were in service; in the Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 the British and French met the old smooth-bore fortress guns of Russia with rifled artillery, and the advantage in range was plain, after which the rifled field gun slowly displaced the smooth-bore and became the new standard of European field warfare. The Taiping had very few rifled guns. At the start the fighting was done with cold arms, broadswords, spears, pitchforks and javelins, with matchlock and flintlock hunting guns and swivel pieces; when the movement took Nanjing in 1853 it captured the bronze and iron guns, swivels, powder and ammunition that the Qing and the local officials had stored, to a count of several hundred, but most were short smooth-bored pieces that fired flat, with limited range, and the Taiping had neither trained gunners nor a common doctrine of shooting, so the guns were set up wherever they pleased on the ramparts or in the camp. A crowded body on the rampart simply had no answer to such old guns when accurate fire came in from long range. The Qing side went the other way: after the Second Opium War from 1860, large quantities of foreign muskets and guns were bought through the foreign firms in Shanghai, the Suzhou arsenal was set up in 1863, the Jiangnan Arsenal opened in 1865 and the Tientsin arsenal followed in 1867, and rifled guns and foreign muskets were gradually issued to the Xiang and Huai armies and formed into artillery units. Beyond that, the siege equipment of the time included ladders, battering rams, ditches, mines and explosive charges, and the Xiang army once carried walled towns in Jiangxi such as Ji'an, Ruizhou and Fuzhou by blowing them up from a mine. On the river the Taiping gathered several hundred boats in the lower Yangtze and fought as a floating corps, while the Qing had the Yangtze fleet and the Xiang river force; movement depended on grain depots, labour gangs and canal transport, and the Taiping met their needs by levying grain and keeping a sacred treasury. Horses were a resource both sides lacked at the outset: the Taiping cavalry was drawn mostly from the old Guangdong and Guangxi ranks and from animals levied locally, and the Xiang army likewise relied on light mounted columns for pursuit.
tactics: 太平軍初期的戰法以流動與奇襲為主：靠黨成軍、避實擊虛，以冷兵器大軍在局部形成優勢後一氣攻城，攻城時用穴地挖道爆破配合雲梯突進，一八五二年攻桂林三月不下的教訓，遂使其後攻城更倚重迂迴與滲透。佔城之後轉為守城，以城頭抬炮與火槍齊射、城內街壘與援軍反擊為主；一旦糧道被斷，便退走他處，重視流動而輕於久守。清軍方面，綠營與八旗守城守關，團練練勇擔任野戰；曾國藩治湘軍講究結壘紮穩，先立營寨、掘壕、佈哨而後進，不爭一城一地之得失，以火槍齊射配合抬炮近射支援冷兵器衝鋒。1860年代後洋槍隊與洋砲加入，攻堅技術為之一變：線膛砲在數里外對準城牆缺口與城頭砲位逐段射擊，使守軍頭目不能抬身，步槍排槍隨後抵近城根，再以壕溝、地道與爆破配合突入。1863年蘇州、1864年天京兩役，湘淮軍依此法攻堅，太平軍在城頭的密集隊形屢被遠程砲火壓散，城頭抬炮失去還手能力，攻守形勢因此逆轉。天京之役中，湘軍以大砲連日轟擊北城、掘壕逼近並施以爆破，終至城破。
tacticsEn: The Taiping method in the early years was movement and surprise. They formed up from their sworn bands, avoided what was strong and struck what was weak, concentrated cold-armed masses locally to gain the advantage of numbers at one point, and went in on a city in a single rush; for siege they used saps, digging in under the walls and blowing them up, with ladders going up at the same time, and the lesson of the three fruitless months at Guilin in 1852 taught them to rely afterwards on turning movements and infiltration. Once they held a city they turned to defending it, with swivel guns and musket volleys from the ramparts, barricades in the streets and counterstrokes by relief columns; and when the road to their grain was cut they moved away, valuing mobility more than a prolonged defence. On the Qing side the banner troops and the Green Standard held towns and passes, and the militias and drill corps did the field work. Zeng Guofan taught the Xiang army to entrench and hold firm: raise the camp, dig the ditch, set the pickets, and only then advance, conceding no town or position out of haste, with musket volleys and the close fire of the swivel guns supporting the charge of cold-armed infantry. After 1860 the foreign rifle corps and foreign guns changed the technique of assault once more. The rifled gun was laid on the breaches in the wall and on the gun positions of the defenders, section by section, from a distance of several li, so that the men on the ramparts could not raise their heads; the muskets in rank came up to the foot of the wall afterwards, and the sappers followed with ditches, mines and explosives. At Suzhou in 1863 and at Tianjing in 1864 the Xiang and Huai armies assaulted in this manner, and the crowded formations of the Taiping on the ramparts were broken again and again by the long-range artillery, while the swivel guns on the walls lost the power to answer, so that the balance of the attack and the defence turned. In the action at Tianjing the Xiang army shelled the northern wall day after day with heavy guns, pushed their ditches forward and used explosive charges, and the city was taken in the end.
data: 可核對的時間與數字如下。起義於一八五〇年一月十一日於廣西桂平縣金田村舉旗；一八五一年三月二十三日永安封王、建號太平天國、定都永安州。一八五一年九月至一八五二年四月攻桂林，三月不下而退，兵員折損頗重。一八五二年九月蕭朝貴攻衡州中炮陣亡，同年十二月太平軍攻入湖北武昌。一八五三年一月十二日攻陷南京，三月定都天京，五月林鳳祥、李開芳率軍北伐，十二月至天津獨流、靜海，因糧匱而退，一八五五年主將兵敗被執；同年西征展開，一八五五年石達開取武昌、漢陽，一八五六年石達開、彭玉麟於湖口、九江大破湘軍，湘軍水師精銳盡喪。一八五六年天京變亂，楊秀清被殺、韋昌輝被誅，石達開率眾出走；一八五九年洪秀全封洪仁玕、李秀成、陳玉成。一八六一年九月安慶陷落，一八六三年十二月蘇州陷落，同年六月石達開於大渡河被俘並在成都被處死，一八六四年六月洪秀全病逝於天京，同年七月十九日天京陷落。太平軍前後攻克城池六百餘座，版圖遍及十八省，治下蘇浙贛皖一帶人口近三千萬，戰事自起義至天京陷落凡十四年，亦有記為十三年者。兵力各家記載懸殊，太平軍鼎盛時常稱百萬，較可靠的估計約十數萬至數十萬，其中真正可用之精銳遠少於此數；湘軍出師時不足一萬，鼎盛時十餘萬；淮軍與常勝軍合計亦不過數萬。軍費方面，清廷每年用於平叛的支出以數千萬兩計，厘金之徵遂成為主要財源。
dataEn: The dates and figures that can be checked run as follows. The rising was raised at Jintian in the county of Guiping, Guangxi, on the eleventh of January 1850. On the twenty-third of March 1851 the princes were enfeoffed at Yongan, the state of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom was proclaimed, and Yonganzhou was made the capital. The siege of Guilin lasted from September 1851 to April 1852 and was abandoned after three months with heavy losses. In September 1852 Xiao Chaogui was killed by a cannon shot at Hengzhou, and in December of the same year the Taiping took Wuchang in Hubei. Nanjing fell on the twelfth of January 1853; Tianjing was made the capital in March; and in May Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang marched north with the northern expedition, reaching Duli and Jinghai outside Tianjin in December before turning back for want of grain, their commanders being taken after their defeat in 1855. The western campaign opened in the same year; in 1855 Shi Dakai took Wuchang and Hanyang, and in 1856 Shi Dakai and Peng Yulin destroyed the Xiang army at Hukou and Jiujiang, the river force of the Xiang being almost annihilated. The Tianjing incident came in 1856, with Yang Xiuqing killed and Wei Changhui executed, and Shi Dakai left with a great part of the army. In 1859 Hong Xiuquan enfeoffed Hong Rengan, Li Xiucheng and Chen Yucheng. Anqing fell in September 1861, Suzhou in December 1863, and in June of that year Shi Dakai was taken at the Dadu River and executed at Chengdu. Hong Xiuquan died of illness at Tianjing in June 1864, and the city fell on the nineteenth of July. The Taiping took six hundred and more cities, its power reached across eighteen provinces, and the population under its rule in the rich provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi and Anhui was close to thirty million. The war ran fourteen years from the rising to the fall of Tianjing, though some accounts give thirteen. The numbers of troops differ wildly between sources: the Taiping at their height are commonly said to have numbered a million, while a more defensible estimate is somewhere between a hundred thousand and several hundred thousand, and the number of men actually fit for service was far below even that; the Xiang army went into the field with fewer than ten thousand and reached a hundred and some thousand at its height; and the Huai army together with the Ever Victorious Army never together exceeded a few tens of thousands. On cost, the court spent tens of millions of taels a year on the suppression, and the levy of likin became the main source of revenue.
cause: 起義的直接背景是鴉片戰爭前後的財政崩解與廣西的災荒。一八四〇年代鴉片戰爭的賠款與捐派攤到沿海各省，銀荒與糧價牽動全國；一八四七年之後廣東、廣西、湖南連年水旱，廣西受災最重，饑民大批流入紫荊山、大藤峒等山區，靠採食、傳教與結社維生，地方團練與官府屢次清剿。一八四三年科舉失意的洪秀全重讀勸世良言一類的書卷，仿其中語句立拜上帝會，宣稱上帝獨一、天父天兄救贖；一八四四年馮雲山入廣西紫荊山傳教，會眾在官府查禁下轉入秘密；一八四六年兩廣總督衙門查禁各類教會與結社，洪秀全避入廣西。一八四九年他回廣東花縣辦團，於金田一帶聚眾，同年廣西大藤峒一帶的農民抗稅起義被鎮壓，更刺激會眾武裝自保。一八五〇年初會眾集於桂平紫荊山，決定起兵。宗教層面上，拜上帝會以救贖的語言聚人心，卻保留客家與兩廣民間信仰的內容，組織嚴密而以洪氏為核心；政治層面上，滿清入主後的旗民畛域、官府對秘密結社的嚴厲打壓、地方吏治的苛索與糧餉攤派，構成逼反的推力。
causeEn: The immediate background of the rising was the financial dislocation that followed the Opium War and the famine in Guangxi. The indemnities and the surtaxes of the 1840s fell on the coastal provinces, and the shortage of silver and the rise of grain prices were felt everywhere. From 1847 onwards Guangdong, Guangxi and Hunan were visited year after year by flood and drought, and Guangxi suffered worst: the hungry moved in thousands into the Zijing and Dateng mountains, living on what they could gather, on preaching and on sworn association, and the local militias and the authorities hunted them down again and again. In 1843 Hong Xiuquan, disappointed in the examinations, read once more at the Christian tracts of the kind that includes the Good Words to Admit the Way of Salvation and modelled his society on their language, proclaiming that there is one God above and that redemption comes through the Heavenly Father and the Heavenly Brother. In 1844 Feng Yunshan took the preaching into the Zijing mountains of Guangxi, and the members of the society, under pressure from the ban on secret sects, went underground. In 1846 the offices of the Governor-General of the Two Guangs moved against the churches and the sworn societies, and Hong Xiuquan withdrew into Guangxi. In 1849 he went back to Huaxian in Guangdong to gather the people, and in the same year the peasant rising against taxation at Dateng in Guangxi was put down, which drove the members of the society further towards armed self-protection. At the beginning of 1850 the members gathered at Zijing near Guiping and resolved to rise. On the religious level the society drew people together with the language of redemption while keeping much of the content of Hakka and Cantonese popular belief, tightly organised and centred on the Hong family; on the political level the divisions between banner people and Han people under the Qing, the harsh suppression of secret societies, the oppressive collection of revenue and taxes by local officials and the levies of grain and pay together made the position of the people untenable.
impact: 這場戰爭改寫了清朝的軍制、財政與對外格局。軍制上，團練與練勇由臨時應急變為常設的野戰主力，湘軍、淮軍取代八旗綠營成為野戰骨幹，地方督撫與士紳由此掌握兵權，中央與地方的權力結構為之一變。技術上，太平軍在冷兵器與舊式抬炮上對線膛砲、洋槍的無力，使清廷在六十年代加速引進與仿製近代火砲，一八六三年蘇州洋炮局、一八六五年江南製造總局、一八六六年籌辦的福州船政局、一八六七年天津機器局相繼開辦，洋務自此起步。財政上，厘金由軍需應急轉為長期稅源，全國稅制與漕運體系為之重整，晚清財政的倚賴與積弊同時加深。對外關係上，第二次鴉片戰爭與本戰事交錯，英法在沿海的干涉與清廷的內戰互相牽制，近代化的嘗試在內憂外患之中被迫加速。軍事思想上，本戰役確立了以火砲射程與精確度制壓密集步兵的道理，晚清軍書與將領對結壘、掘壕、封鎖線的推崇多以此役為範本；太平軍以流動取勝而攻城失利、久守無援的經驗，亦成為其後剿捻與西北平亂中清廷改採堵剿與遠程火砲攻寨的理由。戰後江南、江西、安徽一帶的生產與漕運長期失衡，復甦遲緩，地方社會的宗族與團練勢力在此役之後進一步坐大。
impactEn: This war rewrote the military system, the finances and the foreign relations of the Qing. In the military sphere the militia and the drill corps changed from improvised measures of emergency into permanent field armies; the Xiang and Huai armies displaced the banner troops and the Green Standard as the backbone of the field forces; the provincial governors and the gentry took the army into their own hands, and the distribution of power between the centre and the localities was altered accordingly. On the technical side, the helplessness of cold arms and old swivel guns in the face of rifled artillery and foreign muskets pushed the court to bring in and copy modern guns faster in the 1860s: the Suzhou arsenal in 1863, the Jiangnan Arsenal in 1865, the Foochow shipyard, begun in 1866, and the Tientsin arsenal in 1867, and the self-strengthening movement began from there. Financially, likin passed from an expedient levy for war finance into a standing source of revenue, the tax system and the canal transport of the whole empire were reorganised, and the dependence and the corruption of late Qing finance both deepened. In foreign relations the Second Opium War and this war ran into each other, British and French interference on the coast was tangled with the civil war of the court, and the attempt at modernisation was forced to speed up in the midst of disorder at home and pressure from abroad. In military thought the war settled the argument that dense infantry could be beaten by the reach and the accuracy of guns, and the Qing military writers and officers drew most of their advocacy of entrenchment, of ditches and of blockade lines from this campaign. The Taiping lesson as well, that mobility could win a battle while the assault on a walled city and a long defence without relief could lose a war, was the reason why the suppression of the Nian and the north-west campaigns were later run as blockades fought with long-range guns against the forts. In the provinces of the lower Yangtze, of Jiangxi and of Anhui the production and the canal transport of the districts that had been fought over stayed out of balance for a long while after the war, and the clans and the village militias of the countryside grew stronger still in the years that followed.
result: 一八六四年七月十九日，天京被湘軍攻破，太平天國政權覆亡，延續十四年的戰爭至此大局底定。洪秀全已於同年六月在城中病逝；幼天王洪天貴福出走廣西，同年十月在桂平被擒遭誅；忠王李秀成被俘後在南京遇害；翼王石達開早於一八六三年六月在大渡河被俘並在成都受刑。餘部在湖南、廣西、貴州、江西一帶的散兵與游勇仍抵抗數年，至一八七〇年代初方才被地方團練與清軍肅清。就兵器與戰術而言，結果極為鮮明：攻方在線膛砲與洋槍上取得的射程與精度優勢，決定了蘇州與天京兩役城防的崩解；守方的密集隊形與城頭抬炮在遠程精確射擊面前無從還手，一旦糧道被封、外援被斷，縱有再多兵眾亦難持久。反觀清廷，儘管以慘重代價平定了戰局，卻也由此認清綠營、旗營與舊式抬炮不足以抵禦新式火力，湘淮軍、線膛砲隊、洋槍隊與近代工廠同時壯大，內戰的產物成為日後洋務與新式軍隊的基礎。太平天國一役遂以冷兵器軍隊敗於近代火砲與近代後勤的結局收場，載入晚清軍事史與中國近代史。
resultEn: On the nineteenth of July 1864 Tianjing was taken by the Xiang army, the Taiping state was destroyed, and the war that had run for fourteen years was decided in all essentials. Hong Xiuquan had died of illness in the city in June of that year; the Young King, Hong Tiangui, broke out for Guangxi and was taken and executed at Guiping in October; the Loyal King, Li Xiucheng, was taken prisoner and killed at Nanjing; and the Wing King, Shi Dakai, had been taken at the Dadu River and put to death at Chengdu as early as June 1863. Scattered bands and irregulars of the movement went on fighting in Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou and Jiangxi for several more years, and were not cleared away by the local militias and the Qing armies until the early 1870s. In terms of arms and tactics the outcome is very plain. The advantage in range and accuracy that the attacking side gained with the rifled gun and the foreign musket decided the collapse of the defences at Suzhou and at Tianjing. The crowded formations of the defenders and the swivel guns on the walls had no answer to accurate fire at long range, and once the road to their grain was closed and their relief cut off, no amount of manpower would hold for long. On the other side, though the court had paid a heavy price to settle the war, it had learned that the Green Standard, the banner troops and the old swivel guns were no match for the new firepower; the Xiang and Huai armies, the rifled gun corps, the foreign rifle corps and the modern arsenals all grew at the same time, and what the civil war produced became the foundation of the later self-strengthening movement and of the new-style army. The Taiping war therefore ended with a cold-armed army beaten by modern artillery and modern logistics, and it is written into the military history of the late Qing and the modern history of China.
